title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page. (E, |o|) is a set with a symmetric 'orthogonality' or 'disjointness' relation; the transcription reads this as 'disjonction', which is uncertain. For A ⊆ E write A^o = {x : x |o| a for all a ∈ A}. Σ_E is the system of biorthogonally closed subsets A = A^{oo}, with σ_E : E → Σ_E sending x to {x}^{oo}. (Σ, ≤, C) is a complete lattice with an orthocomplementation C; the transcription's 'opération' is probably a misreading of some 'ortho-' word. In Σ, S |o| T means S ≤ C(T). Σ_E is the 'canonical' complete ortholattice attached to E.

Proposition 2. Let σ : E → Σ be a map. There is an isomorphism φ : Σ_E → Σ with φ∘σ_E = σ if and only if:
(a) x |o| y ⟺ σx |o| σy;
(b) every S ∈ Σ satisfies S = sup{σx : σx ≤ S}, i.e. σ(E) is join-dense in Σ, as the margin note says.
When these hold, φ is unique.

Proof begun on this page:
- Define α(A) = sup_{x∈A} σ(x) on Σ_E. It is monotone, and by (b) it is surjective once one knows β(S) = {x : σx ≤ S} lies in Σ_E.
- To show this, put S' = C S and prove β(S) = β(S')^o:
  - σx ≤ S ⟺ σx |o| S'.
  - By (b), S' = sup σ(β(S')).
  - In an ortholattice, orthogonality to a sup is equivalent to orthogonality to every term.
  - So σx |o| S' ⟺ σx |o| σy for all y ∈ β(S') ⟺ (by (a)) x |o| β(S').
- Hence β(S) is an orthogonal, therefore closed, set.

The next page completes the argument: αβ = id, β is compatible with C, and βα = id via a small lemma.

This is the standard characterisation of the orthogonality-space completion: a Dedekind–MacNeille-type universal property for orthogonality spaces and complete ortholattices.
errors: No mathematical error. The equivalence σx |o| S'_0 ⟺ σx |o| sup S'_0 silently uses the identity C(sup) = inf(C), which holds in any complete ortholattice.
Gap: the claim that α is well defined and order-preserving is said to follow 'using a)', but a) is really only needed for the β-step; monotonicity of α is trivial.

ideas.what: Complete ortholattice Σ_E of biorthogonally closed subsets of an orthogonality space E
Characterisation of when Σ ≅ Σ_E compatibly with σ: σ reflects and preserves orthogonality and has join-dense image
ideas.modern_name: universal property of the MacNeille-type completion of an orthogonality space (join-dense order/ortho embedding)
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacNeille 1937 (completions); MacLaren 1964 / quantum-logic literature for the ortho version

missed.claim: This is evidence of Grothendieck in 1986 working through orthogonality-space / ortholattice formalism of the kind used in quantum logic. Nothing here is mathematically new, but the topic is absent from his published corpus.
missed.quote: on aimerait considérer Σ_E, muni de σ_E : E → Σ_E, comme une "disjonction canonique"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of biographical and historical interest for the context of Chapter IX; no new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: A correct, standard result (the MacNeille-style completion of orthogonality spaces) re-derived by Grothendieck. It is mildly interesting only as an unusual topic for him.
transcription_corrections: 'Comp^o(β(S'))' should read β(S')^o, the orthogonal of β(S') with respect to |o|.
'S' = ∁S' is meant as S' = C(S), the orthocomplement in Σ.
'la bijection α est uniquement déterminée' likely refers to the isomorphism (called φ on the previous page, α here).
'opération(s)' on the previous page is probably a misreading of a term for orthocomplemented complete lattices ('ortho…').
Margin: 'σ(E) est une partie "dense" de Σ, i.e. ∀S∈Σ, S = sup_{x∈E, σx≤S} σx'.
